title: Cluster 02 Drill — Cell and Nuclear Division
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 8 questions · 103 marks · cumulative over Book 3 Cluster 1 + Books 1 and 2
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b) - that is the point of the layout.

Eight questions, not ten, and here is the count. Four learning outcomes, 2(n), 2(o), 2(s) and 2(t), carry thirteen content nodes between them: the cell cycle and its phases, DNA content against chromosome number, the terminology block, the four stages of mitosis against four named structures, cytokinesis in animals and plants, the significance of mitosis, checkpoint dysregulation, prophase I, metaphase I and independent assortment, anaphase I, meiosis II, the significance of meiosis, and the mitosis-against-meiosis comparison. Add eight reach-back nodes - cell signalling from Cluster 1, and from Book 2 the three-level DNA packing ladder, the centromere and telomere as non-coding DNA, semi-conservative replication and proofreading in S phase, non-disjunction and aneuploidy, unequal crossing over and its two products, gene mutation, and germline against somatic - and you have twenty-one. Eight questions at four or more concepts each carry all twenty-one with none repeated. A ninth would have had to re-ask something.

Five real figures, four questions figure-led. Chapter 3.2 is the most graph-driven chapter in Book 3 at 44.1% figure-led, and data and figure interpretation is 33.5% of Book 3 as a whole. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing.

One MCQ only, and it is the specimen's own. Q5(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 17 word for word. You have to judge all four statements and all four options, not pick a letter.

Cumulative, and that is the point. Book 2 taught you what meiotic error causes; Book 3 teaches the event, so the two only make sense held together. Five stems now reach back and not one of them can be answered out of Book 3 alone. Q1(a) needs the three-level packing ladder. Q3(c) needs non-disjunction defined and then applied at both anaphases. Q4(c) needs the centromere in Book 2's own words for non-coding DNA. Q5(d) needs unequal crossing over. Q8 cannot be written without semi-conservative replication, proofreading and gene mutation. Q7(a) still needs the receptor tyrosine kinase and the phosphorylation cascade said cold from Cluster 1. A Book 1 or Book 2 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 2 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Name the exact stage at which each event happens - an examiner report in this file calls vague-across-stages description the commonest failure. Write non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes in full. State both sides of every comparison positively, because schemes reject yes-or-no comparisons twice over. Keep the centromere dividing apart from the kinetochore microtubules shortening. Say cell division, never cell growth, whenever the word uncontrolled is in play. Quote figures off any graph you are told to refer to.
los_html:
Learning outcomes this cluster owns (9477 Core Idea 2)
2(n) the mitotic cell cycle and the main stages of mitosis, including the behaviour of chromosomes, nuclear envelope, cell surface membrane and centriolesQ1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6
2(o) significance of the mitotic cell cycle - growth, repair, asexual reproduction - and the need to regulate it tightlyQ3, Q7, Q8
2(s) the meiotic cell cycle and the main stages of meiosis, same four structuresQ2, Q3, Q5, Q6
2(t) significance of meiosis, including how meiosis and random fertilisation lead to variationQ5, Q6, Q8
reach-back 3(m), 3(o) cell signalling, transduction and amplification (Cluster 1)Q7
reach-back 2(d) the three-level DNA packing ladder, and 2(h) euchromatin against heterochromatin (Book 2)Q1
reach-back 2(h) non-coding DNA: centromeres and telomeres (Book 2)Q4
reach-back 2(a), 2(b) complementary base pairing, semi-conservative replication and proofreading in S phase (Book 2)Q1, Q3, Q8
reach-back 2(k) numerical chromosomal aberration: non-disjunction, aneuploidy, trisomy (Book 2)Q3
reach-back 2(k) structural chromosomal aberration: unequal crossing over, duplication and deletion (Book 2)Q4, Q5
reach-back 2(k), 2(l) gene mutation: substitution, indel, germline against somatic (Book 2)Q8

Nothing from Books 4 to 9, and nothing from Book 3 chapters 3.3 or 3.4. Cancer genetics and stem cells are not studied yet, so no question needs them. Q7(c) goes exactly as far as LO 2(o) goes and stops.
